advances: There is no absolute positive lower-bound constant for the original cubic depth moment at scale \(8^{-(k+1)}\) for arbitrary coordinatewise monotone ternary-cube energies once positive spatial affine tilts are allowed. The exact family below has a complete integer-height table with \(T=\beta=0\), but its spatial support omits an integer point of its convex hull. It therefore blocks this sign extension for arbitrary monotone energies without providing a complete convex lattice counterexample or a disproof of the locked weak Oertel conjecture.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. Accepted fact `11d156df58653939` supplies only the canonical monotone-table and original depth-moment framework, with the weight change stated explicitly above. All combinatorial, probability, halfspace, asymptotic, and convexity assertions used for this counterexample are proved in this packet.
proof:
Fix \(m\ge1\). There are \((4m)!/(m!^2(2m)!)\) distinct permutations because the repeated entries have multiplicities \(m,2m,m\). In particular \(M_m\) is a positive integer. There are at least two distinct permutations, since the defining vector contains both a zero and a two. Hence \(M_m\ge2\) and the integer \(R_m=3^{4m}M_m^3\) is greater than one.

The set \(D_m\) is a downset: if \(\mathbf y\le\mathbf x\) and \(\mathbf x\le\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_m\), then \(\mathbf y\le\mathbf a\). It contains \(\mathbf0\). If \(\mathbf x\le\mathbf y\) and \(\Gamma_m(\mathbf x)=1\), then \(\mathbf y\) cannot belong to \(D_m\), since downward closure would put \(\mathbf x\) in \(D_m\). Thus \(\Gamma_m(\mathbf x)\le\Gamma_m(\mathbf y)\) for every comparable pair, and \(\Gamma_m\) is coordinatewise nondecreasing on the entire ternary cube. Its values are nonnegative integers and \(\Gamma_m(\mathbf0)=0\). With \(T=0\), the inequality \(\Gamma_m(\mathbf x)\le t\le0\) allows exactly \(t=0\) at sites in \(D_m\). This proves the asserted complete height-table identity. The original weight at \((\mathbf x,0)\) is exactly \(R_m^{\sum_i x_i}\).

Every \(\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_m\) has

$$
\sum_{i=1}^k a_i=2m+2m=k,\qquad
\lVert\mathbf a\rVert_2^2=2m+4m=6m.
\tag{1}
$$

For any \(\mathbf x\in D_m\), choose \(\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_m\) with \(\mathbf x\le\mathbf a\). Then \(\sum_i x_i\le k\); if equality holds, the nonnegative differences \(a_i-x_i\) sum to zero, so each difference is zero and \(\mathbf x=\mathbf a\). Therefore the sites of \(D_m\) with coordinate sum \(k\) are exactly \(\mathcal A_m\), and every other site has coordinate sum at most \(k-1\).

Let \(W_m:=M_mR_m^k\) be the total unnormalized weight at \(\mathcal A_m\times\lbrace0\rbrace\), and let \(V_m\) be the total unnormalized weight at its complement in \(A_T\). There are at most \(3^k\) sites in this complement. As \(R_m>1\), each has weight at most \(R_m^{k-1}\), whence

$$
0\le V_m\le3^kR_m^{k-1},\qquad
Z=W_m+V_m,\qquad
\varepsilon_m:=\frac{V_m}{Z}
\le\frac{V_m}{W_m}
\le\frac{3^k}{M_mR_m}=M_m^{-4}.
\tag{2}
$$

Thus the original total probability off the top layer is \(\varepsilon_m\). All top-layer atoms have the same original probability \((1-\varepsilon_m)/M_m\).

For \(\mathbf a,\mathbf b\in\mathcal A_m\), identity (1) gives

$$
\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b
=6m-\frac12\lVert\mathbf a-\mathbf b\rVert_2^2.
\tag{3}
$$

If \(\mathbf b\ne\mathbf a\), the right side is strictly less than \(6m\). The left side is an integer, so \(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b\le6m-1\). Define the closed affine halfspace in the original ambient space by

$$
H_{\mathbf a}:=\lbrace(\mathbf z,s)\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf z\ge6m-\tfrac12\rbrace.
\tag{4}
$$

Its normal is \((\mathbf a,0)\ne\mathbf0\), since \(m\ge1\) and \(\mathbf a\) has nonzero coordinates. Thus (4) is an admissible ambient halfspace even though all atoms have height zero. It contains \((\mathbf a,0)\) because \(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf a=6m\), and it contains no other top-layer atom by (3). All inequalities are strict relative to the threshold for top-layer atoms; hence the use of closed halfspaces causes no boundary ambiguity. Its remaining supported atoms, if any, have total probability at most \(\varepsilon_m\). It follows directly from the original depth definition that

$$
\tau_{p^{(m)}}((\mathbf a,0))
\le\frac{1-\varepsilon_m}{M_m}+\varepsilon_m
\le\frac1{M_m}+\varepsilon_m.
\tag{5}
$$

Every supported point has depth at most one, since every halfspace has probability at most one and the set of halfspaces containing that point is nonempty. Splitting the original moment into the top layer and its complement, and using (2) and (5), therefore gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
M_3(p^{(m)})
&\le(1-\varepsilon_m)\left(\frac1{M_m}+\varepsilon_m\right)^3+\varepsilon_m\\
&\le\left(\frac1{M_m}+M_m^{-4}\right)^3+M_m^{-4}\\
&\le\left(\frac2{M_m}\right)^3+\frac1{M_m^3}
=\frac9{M_m^3}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
$$

The last inequality uses only \(M_m\ge1\). This is a bound on the full original-law moment: no conditioning, replacement law, or restriction of the halfspace family has been used.

For every integer \(r\ge1\), the central binomial coefficient is the largest coefficient of \((1+u)^{2r}\). Indeed, the ratio of consecutive coefficients is \((2r-j)/(j+1)\), which is greater than one for \(j<r\) and at most one for \(j\ge r\). Their sum is \(2^{2r}\), so \(\binom{2r}{r}\ge2^{2r}/(2r+1)\). Applying this with \(r=2m\) and \(r=m\) yields

$$
M_m=\binom{4m}{2m}\binom{2m}{m}
\ge\frac{2^{6m}}{(4m+1)(2m+1)}.
\tag{7}
$$

Combining (6), (7), and \(k=4m\) gives

$$
0\le8^{k+1}M_3(p^{(m)})
\le9\cdot8^{4m+1}\frac{((4m+1)(2m+1))^3}{2^{18m}}
=72\,\frac{((4m+1)(2m+1))^3}{2^{6m}}.
\tag{8}
$$

The ratio of the final expression at \(m+1\) to its value at \(m\) tends to \(1/64<1\); hence it tends to zero. This proves the stated limit and its quantified consequence for every \(\kappa>0\). The logarithm of each spatial weight is \((\log R_m)\sum_i x_i\), whose coefficient in every spatial coordinate is strictly positive. Thus the family has exactly the positive spatial affine tilt at issue.

It remains to check the scope of this counterexample. The uniform average of the vectors in \(\mathcal A_m\) is \(\mathbf1\). To see this exactly, permutation symmetry makes all coordinates of the average equal, and their sum is \(k\) by (1), so each of its \(k\) coordinates equals one. Consequently

$$
(\mathbf1,0)=\frac1{M_m}\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_m}(\mathbf a,0)
\in\operatorname{conv}(A_T)\cap\mathbb Z^{k+1}.
\tag{9}
$$

Every \(\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_m\) has \(m\ge1\) zero coordinates. Thus \(\mathbf1\le\mathbf a\) is false for every such \(\mathbf a\), and the definition of \(D_m\) gives \(\mathbf1\notin D_m\). Therefore \(\Gamma_m(\mathbf1)=1\) and \((\mathbf1,0)\notin A_T\). Equations (9) and this exclusion show the claimed missing integer point. If a convex set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^{k+1}\) had \(K\cap\mathbb Z^{k+1}=A_T\), it would contain every \((\mathbf a,0)\), hence their average \((\mathbf1,0)\), contradicting that equality. In particular the chosen support is not a complete convex lattice support. The energy even fails convex interpolation at these sites: any convex function agreeing with its zero values on \(\mathcal A_m\) would have value at most zero at \(\mathbf1\), whereas \(\Gamma_m(\mathbf1)=1\).

The locked target concerns complete mixed-integer intersections of convex bodies and an existential point with a specified depth. Here the support already fails the necessary convex-hull completeness condition in the discrete table, and the established failure is a lower bound for an auxiliary average cubic moment. No convex body meeting the locked hypotheses has been constructed. Thus this exact family refutes only the proposed uniform moment bound for arbitrary monotone energies with positive spatial tilt; it does not refute the complete convex lattice version of that bound or the weak Oertel conjecture.
statement:
Use the table and original ambient-halfspace moment notation of accepted fact `11d156df58653939`, with the following explicit change of weights. For an integer \(k\ge1\), a coordinatewise nondecreasing function \(\Gamma:\lbrace0,1,2\rbrace^k\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) with \(\Gamma(\mathbf0)=0\), an integer \(T\ge0\), and real numbers \(\beta\ge0\) and \(R>1\), put

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_T&:=\lbrace(\mathbf x,t):\mathbf x\in\lbrace0,1,2\rbrace^k,\ t\in\mathbb Z,\ \Gamma(\mathbf x)\le t\le T\rbrace,\\
Z&:=\sum_{(\mathbf x,t)\in A_T}R^{\sum_{i=1}^k x_i}e^{-\beta t},\qquad
p_{(\mathbf x,t)}:=\frac{R^{\sum_{i=1}^k x_i}e^{-\beta t}}{Z}.
\end{aligned}
$$

For \(\mathbf z\in A_T\), define

$$
\begin{aligned}
\tau_p(\mathbf z)&:=\inf_{H\ni\mathbf z}\sum_{\mathbf v\in A_T\cap H}p_{\mathbf v},\\
M_3(p)&:=\sum_{\mathbf z\in A_T}p_{\mathbf z}\tau_p(\mathbf z)^3,
\end{aligned}
$$

where the infimum is over all closed affine halfspaces \(H=\lbrace\mathbf v\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf v\ge b\rbrace\) with \(\mathbf u\ne\mathbf0\). Thus \(A_T,\tau_p,M_3\) have exactly the meanings in `11d156df58653939`; \(Z,p\) use the displayed spatially tilted weights rather than that fact's weights \(e^{-\beta t}\). No spatially weighted conclusion is imported from that fact. The locked problem's \(n,d,C,\Lambda,S,h_S\) are not redefined.

For every integer \(m\ge1\), let \(k=4m\), let \(\mathcal A_m\) be the set of all distinct coordinate permutations of a vector with \(m\) zeros, \(2m\) ones, and \(m\) twos, and define

$$
\begin{aligned}
M_m&:=|\mathcal A_m|=\frac{(4m)!}{m!^2(2m)!},\\
D_m&:=\lbrace\mathbf x\in\lbrace0,1,2\rbrace^k:\mathbf x\le\mathbf a\text{ coordinatewise for some }\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_m\rbrace,\\
\Gamma_m(\mathbf x)&:=\begin{cases}0,&\mathbf x\in D_m,\\1,&\mathbf x\notin D_m,\end{cases}
\qquad R_m:=3^kM_m^3.
\end{aligned}
$$

Take \(\Gamma=\Gamma_m\), \(T=\beta=0\), and \(R=R_m\), and denote the resulting probability by \(p^{(m)}\). Then \(\Gamma_m\) satisfies all the stated monotonicity and integrality assumptions, \(R_m\) is an integer greater than one, \(A_T=D_m\times\lbrace0\rbrace\), and

$$
M_3(p^{(m)})\le\frac9{M_m^3},\qquad
8^{k+1}M_3(p^{(m)})
\le72\,\frac{((4m+1)(2m+1))^3}{2^{6m}}
\longrightarrow0.
$$

Consequently, for every \(\kappa>0\), some member of this family satisfies \(M_3(p^{(m)})<\kappa8^{-(k+1)}\). However, the integer point \((\mathbf1,0)\) lies in \(\operatorname{conv}(A_T)\setminus A_T\), so this support is not the complete integer intersection of any convex set in \(\mathbb R^{k+1}\).
